detail.longDescription: One of the chores of git is to move uncommitted hunks into the right commit. To illustrate (by printing the diff on top of the commit stack): In this example, the foo-change belongs in the foo-commit, which is HEAD~2, pointed to by branch-foo, which several other local branches are based on. Problem: The traditional ways to do this are laborious and have unwanted side-effects (see goals below). Has anyone come up with a tool that does precisely this, and does it well? Goals: Single-step workflow (preferably atomic): I'm prone to be interrupted. No invisible staging: I can tolerate if the tool automates creating a temporary commit (although I prefer not, as it affects the point below, not to mention commit-hooks), but staging is a source of mistakes for me. This disqualifies git-absorb. I don't want to type things like HEAD~2, as that number changes by the minute. Must update refs (like git rebase --update-refs ) Assume I'm compiling: No touching of the workspace allowed. I only know of git-revise that accomplishes this. What I currently do: I commit the changes as "asdf", interactively git-revise them into the right commit, and I have to use and maintain a custom fork of git-revise that also updates the affected refs.
